own_solution.law: Energy conservation gives v_escape = sqrt(2GM/R). For a uniform sphere, M = (4π/3)ρR³, so v_escape is proportional to R sqrt(ρ). Using Earth as the reference gives v_escape = 11.19(3390/6371)sqrt(3.93/5.51) = 5.03 km/s.
assumptions: The probe travels without further propulsion after launch and reaches infinity with zero limiting speed.
The probe's gravitational effect on the planet is negligible.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TC598 and T39C4 replace the explicit 310 km increment in their corresponding variants with an unquantified 'little', violating the requirement that variants preserve the same number and unit.

counterexamples: An increment of 10 km could reasonably be described as 'a little', so TC598 and T39C4 do not specify the same increment as the 310 km variants.
notes: The base escape-speed problem is well-posed. Probe mass cancels between kinetic and gravitational potential energies. Moon changes are disconnected because other bodies' gravitational pulls are explicitly ignored; earlier simulations do not change the present planet. Adding the planetary layer changes its radius to 3700 km while preserving density, giving 11.19(3700/6371)sqrt(3.93/5.51) = 5.49 km/s. The planetary-layer statements describe a physical update rather than contradictory simultaneous radii. The invalid verdict concerns the required equivalence of sentence variants.
